description: Hand-curated, domain-agnostic adaptive rules shipped with TestForge to give new deployments useful generation guidance on day one. These rules start at lower confidence (0.6) and decay faster (21-day half-life) than learned rules, so they retire naturally as feedback-derived rules accumulate.

rules.rule_text: Every test step must specify an observable, measurable expected result. Avoid vague outcomes like "works correctly."
Each test case should verify one logical behavior. Split cases with multiple unrelated pass/fail conditions.
List preconditions as concrete, verifiable states (e.g., "User is logged in as non-admin"), not as setup actions to perform.
Each step should describe one user action and its expected result. Don't combine multiple actions into one step.
When a test creates, modifies, or deletes data, include a cleanup step that returns the system to its pre-test state.
For requirements with numeric limits or ranges, include boundary tests on both sides of each limit: at the limit, one below, and one above.
When a requirement defines accepted input formats, include at least one negative case with malformed input and verify the specific error handling.
Include test cases for empty, null, and absent inputs whenever a field, parameter, or collection is involved.
Generated sets should include at least one happy-path, one negative, and one boundary case unless the requirement has no failure or boundary conditions.
Expected results must be verifiable by direct observation, not by interpretation ("Toast displays text X" not "User is informed of success").
For authentication-related requirements, include a session expiry test verifying behavior when a session is invalidated mid-operation.
For API validation requirements, every failure-path test must verify response status code, error body structure, and absence of partial state mutation.
